questions.q: What is the main difference between Azure Monitor Metrics and Azure Monitor Logs?
options: Metrics are lightweight numerical time series; logs are detailed records queried with KQL
Metrics are for Windows resources only; logs are for Linux resources only
They are two names for the exact same data store
Logs are collected automatically; metrics require custom code
questions.explain: Metrics are numerical time series collected automatically and cheaply. Logs are detailed structured or free-text records stored in a Log Analytics workspace and queried with KQL.

questions.q: What does Metrics Explorer let you do without writing a query?
options: Chart a resource's metrics by picking a resource, metric, and aggregation
Edit the resource's source code
Rewrite KQL queries automatically
Delete old log data
questions.explain: Metrics Explorer is a point-and-click charting tool in the Azure portal — no KQL or any query language is needed to plot a metric.

questions.q: Northbridge wants to track 'CartAbandonmentCount,' a number tied to its own checkout business logic. What would it use?
options: A platform metric, since Azure already tracks this automatically
A custom metric, emitted by the application itself
The Activity Log
Metrics Explorer's built-in aggregation list
questions.explain: Platform metrics only cover what Azure already knows about a resource (CPU, requests, etc.). Business-specific numbers like cart abandonment require a custom metric emitted by the application.

questions.q: What is a 'dimension' in the context of an Azure Monitor metric?
options: A separate billing category for metrics
A property you can split a metric chart by, such as HTTP status code
The time range selector
A type of alert action
questions.explain: Dimensions let you segment a metric — for example splitting total Requests by status code to isolate the share that are 5xx errors.

questions.q: Why does Azure Monitor keep metrics and logs in separate stores rather than one?
options: Because metrics are deprecated and being phased out
Because logs only work with Application Insights, not Azure Monitor
Because they serve different jobs — metrics for cheap, fast alerting; logs for detailed after-the-fact investigation
Because Microsoft requires separate Azure subscriptions for each
questions.explain: Metrics answer 'how much, right now' cheaply, which is what you wire alerts to. Logs answer 'what exactly happened,' which is what you query once an alert fires — different jobs, different storage trade-offs.
